rv.q: As a dramatic simulacrum of the past two decades of western politics, David Edgar's play explores some pressing questions where the real-world stakes could not be higher. It's unfortunate that these stakes are rarely matched by the dramatic ones.
The writing is vigorous, the situations taut in this loftily ambitious work.

cn.t: David Edgar's political thriller earns praise for its timely exploration of post-truth campaign tactics, as two Western strategists navigate a ruthless Eastern European election marked by manipulation and murky ethics.
